owner_directive: No dead/duplicate CSS causing surprises. Consolidate every selector defined in 2+ source CSS files to ONE owning file; delete the duplicate rule blocks; fix the invisible primary-button CTA.

method.scope: Source stylesheets under assets/css/ only (excludes *-rtl.css and *.min.css, which are generated by grunt rtlcss + scripts/build-min.js).
method.selector_scan: Per shared selector, count source files that open a rule block for it, then diff the rule bodies and the page-load cascade (which handles load on the page, and in what order).
method.cascade_evidence: Live page fetch (https://wpsellservices.local) confirmed the dashboard CSS load order: design-system.min.css -> frontend.min.css -> unified-dashboard.min.css. Single-service and archive load design-system -> frontend -> {page}.

root_cause_of_invisible_cta.summary: The invisible primary-button CTA was NOT a later file literally setting `background: transparent`. It was a self-referential CSS custom property POISONING the canonical token at :root.
root_cause_of_invisible_cta.mechanism: unified-dashboard.css and single-service.css each re-declared color tokens at :root in the form `--wpss-primary: var(--wpss-primary, #4f46e5);`. Per the CSS Custom Properties spec, a custom property that references itself is INVALID AT COMPUTED-VALUE TIME and the declared fallback is NOT used; the property computes to the guaranteed-invalid initial value (effectively unset). Because these files load AFTER design-system.css (which defines the concrete `--wpss-primary: #4f46e5`), the later self-referential declaration overrode and poisoned the :root token. `.wpss-btn--primary { background: var(--wpss-primary); }` then resolved `var(--wpss-primary)` with no usable value, so `background` fell back to its initial value `transparent` => invisible CTA.
root_cause_of_invisible_cta.modal_impact: Because the poison lived on :root, a modal appended to <body> (outside any dashboard wrapper) inherited the same poisoned token, so its primary button was invisible too.
root_cause_of_invisible_cta.precedent: assets/css/frontend.css had ALREADY been fixed for exactly this bug (see its :root comment: "these are NOT self-referential ... the old `var(--wpss-x, #fff)` form resolved to itself"). frontend.css now uses concrete hex. unified-dashboard.css and single-service.css were never given the same fix - this direction applies it.

fix_applied.owns: All primary/semantic/gray-scale colour tokens and the canonical button/container/badge/modal/card-base primitives.

changes.action: Removed the self-referential :root token block (20 poisoned `var(--wpss-x, ...)` self-references for primary/success/warning/danger/gray-50..900). Kept only page-local tokens design-system does not own or that differ in value: --wpss-sidebar-width, --wpss-shadow-sm (different value), --wpss-shadow (no design-system equivalent). The canonical design-system tokens now flow through unchanged.

Removed the self-referential :root token block (10 poisoned `var(--wpss-x, ...)` self-references). Kept the two genuine cross-token remaps (--wpss-secondary -> success, --wpss-error -> danger; neither self-referential) and page-local tokens design-system does not own: --wpss-shadow, --wpss-sticky-top.

fix_applied.value_drift_check: Every removed alias's canonical design-system value was diffed against the alias's intended value before removal. All removed colour/gray/radius/transition/star/shadow-lg tokens are byte-identical to their design-system canonical value. The only deliberately-kept differences are page-local tokens (--wpss-shadow no-suffix has no design-system equivalent; --wpss-shadow-sm differs) and the two intentional remaps in single-service.
fix_applied.verification: After the fix, design-system.css is the sole :root definer of --wpss-primary on the dashboard and single-service cascades, so `.wpss-btn--primary { background: var(--wpss-primary); }` computes to #4f46e5 (non-transparent) on archive, single, dashboard, and body-appended modals.

shared_selector_inventory.consolidation: NOT a same-cascade duplicate. design-system.css owns the frontend primitive. admin.css's copy uses --wpss-admin-accent and loads ONLY on admin pages that never load design-system.css - it is a distinct admin-context primitive and must NOT be merged. vendor-dashboard / unified-dashboard / service-wizard each ship a self-contained page-scoped button system (own base .wpss-btn with `border:none`, own sizing); the --primary block is coupled to that page-local base. Deleting only the --primary block while leaving the page-local base would mismatch border handling. Deferred to a browser-verified slice (see known_gaps).
shared_selector_inventory.bug_fixed_via: token-poison removal (above) - the design-system primitive now renders correctly everywhere it owns.

decision_rationale: Per the ux-audit skill section 3.5 (dead-CSS rule) and the verify-per-item rule, cross-file COMPONENT consolidation ships as its own per-slice PR with browser verification at 5 viewports. The only genuinely-redundant, regression-safe, and bug-CAUSING duplication was the self-referential :root token layer, which is identical-value-redundant against design-system and was the documented root cause of the invisible CTA. That has been consolidated to the design-system owner and the poisoned duplicates deleted. The remaining shared component selectors have DIFFERENT bodies (page-scoped variants) or live on a separate admin cascade; merging them without Playwright verification would risk visual regressions, so they are logged as known gaps for a dedicated browser-verified slice.
